# .github/workflows/

- `ci.yml`: jobs `rust` (build the helper wasms, `cargo test --locked` in `contract/` with a sha256-pinned near-sandbox binary, the committed-wasm checks, `cargo deny` advisories), `ts` (frozen install, `pnpm audit`, `tsc`, app build, `pnpm -r test`, `pnpm vectors`, `pnpm demo:local`, the docs checks and `.github/workflows/ci-config.test.mjs`), `oracle` (`ORACLE=1 pnpm --filter @tender/app test`) and `secrets` (gitleaks over the full git history) run on every push to `main` and every pull request. Every action is pinned to a commit SHA and every downloaded tool is checked against a sha256 before it runs; `ci-config.test.mjs` fails when one is not. The `repro` job runs only from a manual dispatch with the input `ref` (the commit the release candidate was built from): it checks that exact commit out with full history, runs `cargo near build reproducible-wasm` and prints the `sha256` of `tender.wasm` in the run summary. A dispatch without `ref` skips it.
- `keeper.yml`: scheduled job for sale #2 (closes 2026-11-17T12:00Z): every 10 minutes from 12:00Z it runs `pnpm keeper`, which decides from the chain what is due (`open`, `reveal` of every bid that decrypts and matches its commitment, `finalize`, payout retries, or `cancel` when the rules allow it) and sends what is due, turn by turn, until it must wait; every 30 minutes on 2026-11-18 and 19 for the reveal deadline and payouts. Uses repository secrets `KEEPER_ACCOUNT_ID` / `KEEPER_PRIVATE_KEY` (a function-call key limited to the Tender contract and the methods `open`, `reveal`, `finalize`, `cancel`). A manual dispatch defaults to view-only (`dry_run`). Every transaction is listed with its explorer link in the run summary. Anyone can also call `open`, `reveal`, `finalize` and `cancel` by hand.
